Aleksandr Ivanovich Gavrilov (1891 — 21 November 1919) was a Russian revolutionary and Bolshevik who fought for Soviet rule in Siberia. He served on the executive committee of the Peasants' Section of the All-Russian Central Executive Committee (VTsIK) of the RSFSR, the delegate of the 2nd All-Russian Congress of Soviets and the 4th All-Russian Extraordinary Congress of Soviets. In 1919, he and his brother Vasily were executed by Kolchak's White Army.
Biography
Aleksandr Ivanovich Gavrilov was born in Novy Tartas village, Kainsky uyezd, Tomsk Governorate, to merchant and old Saint-Petersburg's metalworker Ivan Stepanovich Gavrilov and Sekletinya Ivanovna Gavrilova (Tikhonova). The family of Gavrilov's father were exiled to Siberia because of revolutionary activity.
Aleksandr attended the village school then worked in farming.
Aleksandr married Aleksandra Dmitrievna Gavrilova (m.name Shashova), and they had three  children.
The Revolution of 1905 and the peasant movement of 1906 led to an influx of exiled Bolsheviks to Siberia. With their support were creating Marxist groups and youth institutes, which grew to party organizations. There also were underground organizations in the village Spasskoe, Kainsky uyezd Ust-Tartassk volost, Tomsk guberniya, where Gavrilov was selling in groceries (on the secret address) of multiple store cooperatives, which owned all the values of society.  Gavrilov was also a student of the Blustein (Blaustein) private pharmacies.
Political activities
Some time in the early 1900s, Alexander and Vasily Gavrilov became active members in the underground Bolshevik movement. The brothers in 1905 would then move to Spassoke Village, where they would work to spread the influence of the movement underground.
Starting in 1913, Gavrilov got a job as a worker in a locksmith shop. Subsequently, moving to Kainsk, where he began leading propaganda campaigns for the revolution. Due to his activities in the Oblast, he was suspected by the Royal security forces of being a revolutionary, which forced him to move to Omsk, where he found work on the railroad as a locksmith.  After four years of working at the railroad, he was promoted to a metalworker-gauger. Due to his underground revolutionary activities, he would move from Kainsk, Spasskoe, Tashkent, and then find work within the Ural factories. He would work many professions during this time, including being a locksmith, a machinist in a creamery, and farm work.
He was involved in investigations twice because of political activities, later joining the Socialist-Revolutionary Party. He would become a member of the 1st Volost Kainsk Soviet of Deputies and the Tomsk Governorate Congress of Soviets. On March 25, 1917, after being unanimously elected at the congress of volost representatives of Kainsk uyezd, he was seletected by the volost committee to represent them at the congress of peasant deputies in the city of Omsk.
The manual for organizations of Soviet authority recalled him. Being a delegate from the Urals at the 2nd All-Russian Congress of Soviets, he was then elected to the All-Russian Central Executive Committee.
In March 1918, delegated with the final vote of Soviet of Workers, peasant, military, cossack, and Muslim deputies of Tashkent, Sirdarya region, on the 4th Congress of Soviets in Moscow. Due to his rising poltiical authroity, on April 15, 1918 he became a participant of the executive committee of the peasant Section All-Russian Central Executive Committee. Other deligates includeded, with P.A. Kudryavtsev, who represented the Tashkent Oblast Soviet (Syrdarya region) and Zharkov who was the chairman of the Turkestan Soviet Committee.

File:О докладе А И Гаврилова по Туркестнскому окружному артиллерийскому управлению.jpg|Certificate of Report on the Turkestan District Artillery Administration
At the 5th All-Russian Congress of Soviets (July 6 — 10, 1918), Gavrilov was elected as a member of the All-Russian Central Executive Committee (VTsIK) of the RSFSR.
After meeting with Vladimir Lenin, Gavrilov, as a member of the peasant section of the VTsI, was sent to Irkutsk to participate in underground spying against Alexander Kolchak's reactionary dictatorship. The Revolutionary Government sent him to Omsk to establish a Soviet Deputation. In late 1918, he traveled to Manchuria and then returned to Irkutsk, where he was arrested by Kolchak's counterintelligence.
While hiding in Irkutsk, his passport listed him as Alexander Ivanovich Fedotov.
— From a letter by his younger sister, Taisia Ivanovna Selezneva (Gavrilova). 1969 He was transported to Kainsk on June 26 (?) 1919, an hour before the planned uprising. After the failure of the uprising on June 24, he obtained a severe head wound and was placed into solitary confinement. While in confinement, he was starved, shackled, and not given water. ON November 21, 1919, he was taken out among 13 other political prisoners for their execution on the banks of the Om River. Instead of a firring squad they were brough before the loacl villiagers and hacked to death with sabers and tossed into a hole in the ice within the river. On December 1, 1919 Kainsk was taken by the Red Army and the bodies of the victums were recovered and buired with military honors. Gavrilov rests with the other prisoners executed in the village of Novy Tartas.
Notice. The Kainsk Investigative Commission, bringing to the attention of the town and district population the list of those arrested, requests that you immediately provide written or verbal information that may serve as evidence against any of those arrested for harmful and criminal behavior as an agent of the Soviet government or actions against the Siberian Provisional Government.
The Commission warns the population that any of those arrested against whom there is insufficient evidence, and for whom no such evidence is presented by any citizen, will be released due to insufficient evidence of guilt.
Furthermore, the Commission requests that information be provided regarding individuals not included in the list, in order to bring them to justice as quickly as possible.
Applications are accepted at the Commission's office... Note: Lists of newly arrested individuals will be published additionally.

Memory
The obelisk with inscription: «Alexander Ivanovich Gavrilov and Vasily Ivanovich Gavrilov, Red Partisans, brutally tortured to death by Kolchakists in November 1919» was established in Aleksandr and Vasily Gavrilov's motherland, in the garden of 8(7)-year School, village Novy Tartas in 1953. In 1979, the monument was moved and reconstructed during the rebuilding of the new school, located in the center of village.
The executive committee of the Vengerovsky District Soviet of Workers' Deputies, in the brothers Gavrilov's motherland of Novy Tartas, Vengerovsky District, decided to name a street «Gavrilov Brothers».
